name: Caro-Kann: Main Line
description: The fundamental Caro-Kann setup. Black prepares ...d5 on the next move with a rock-solid pawn structure, avoiding the trapped light-squared bishop of the French Defense.
keyIdeas: Prepare ...d5 to contest White's e4 pawn
Keep light-squared bishop diagonal open
Aim for resilient, symmetrical pawn structures

name: Caro-Kann: Advance Variation (Short System)
description: White locks the center with 3.e5. Black actively develops the light-squared bishop to f5 outside the pawn chain before locking the solid e6-d5-c6 chain.
keyIdeas: Develop bishop to f5 before playing ...e6
Undermine White's d4 pawn base with ...c5 and ...Qb6
Nigel Short's refined Be2 system for White

name: Caro-Kann: Classical (Capablanca)
moves: 1. e4 c6 2. d4 d5 3. Nc3 dxe4 4. Nxe4 Bf5 5. Ng3 Bg6 6. h4 h6 7. Nf3 Nd7
description: José Raúl Capablanca's legendary fortress. Black exchanges on e4, develops ...Bf5, and shelters the bishop on g6, deflecting White's kingside thrusts.
keyIdeas: Retreat bishop safely to g6 after 5.Ng3
Prevent bishop traps with ...h6
Develop knight to d7 to stop Ne5 invasions

name: Caro-Kann: Modern / Karpov Variation
moves: 1. e4 c6 2. d4 d5 3. Nc3 dxe4 4. Nxe4 Nd7 5. Nf3 Ngf6 6. Nxf6+ Nxf6
description: Anatoly Karpov's premier weapon. Black plays 4...Nd7 preparing ...Ngf6 to recapture on f6 with the knight, avoiding doubled pawns and early tactical vulnerability.
keyIdeas: Recapture on f6 with the knight (...Nxf6)
Maintain flawless pawn structure
Positional maneuvering leading to favorable endgames

name: Caro-Kann: Panov-Botvinnik Attack
moves: 1. e4 c6 2. d4 d5 3. exd5 cxd5 4. c4 Nf6 5. Nc3 e6 6. Nf3 Be7
description: White plays 4.c4 to blast open the center and establish an Isolated Queen's Pawn (IQP), creating dynamic piece pressure and attacking avenues.
keyIdeas: White gains open c- and e-files for piece attacks
Black blockades the d5 square in front of the isolated pawn
Sharp, dynamic play unlike traditional quiet Caro-Kann lines

name: Caro-Kann: Exchange Variation
moves: 1. e4 c6 2. d4 d5 3. exd5 cxd5 4. Bd3 Nc6 5. c3 Nf6 6. Bf4
description: A solid, positional approach. White trades pawns on d5 and controls the central diagonals with Bd3 and Bf4, preventing Black's light-squared bishop from developing easily.
keyIdeas: Control the b1-h7 and c1-h6 diagonals
Play c3 to reinforce d4 against ...Nc6 pressure
Symmetrical pawn structures with subtle positional maneuvering

name: Caro-Kann: Two Knights Variation
moves: 1. e4 c6 2. Nc3 d5 3. Nf3 Bg4 4. h3 Bxf3 5. Qxf3 e6
description: White avoids an early d4, preferring fast piece development. Black pins the f3 knight with 3...Bg4 and trades it to establish a bulletproof pawn chain.
keyIdeas: Pin and trade f3 knight with ...Bg4
Build a rock-solid center with ...e6 and ...d5
White enjoys the bishop pair while Black has pawn harmony

name: Caro-Kann: Fantasy / Maróczy Variation
moves: 1. e4 c6 2. d4 d5 3. f3 dxe4 4. fxe4 e5 5. Nf3 exd4
description: An aggressive, romantic attacking try. White reinforces e4 with 3.f3, aiming to maintain a massive two-pawn center and open the f-file for kingside assault.
keyIdeas: Maintain central pawn duo with f3
Black strikes back immediately with 4...e5!
Wild tactical complications and open kingside files

name: Caro-Kann: Tartakower / Korchnoi Variation
moves: 1. e4 c6 2. d4 d5 3. Nc3 dxe4 4. Nxe4 Nf6 5. Nxf6+ exf6
description: Viktor Korchnoi's fighting choice. Black voluntarily accepts doubled f-pawns after 5...exf6 to achieve rapid piece development and open the e-file.
keyIdeas: Doubled f-pawns compensate with quick piece activation
Open e-file for rooks and active diagonals for bishops
Dynamic imbalance with fighting winning chances

name: Queen's Gambit: Main Line
description: The quintessential classical opening. White challenges Black's central d5 pawn with the c4 wing pawn to build a broad center with e4.
keyIdeas: Undermine Black's d5 anchor
Control the central e4 square
Open the c-file for queenside pressure

name: Queen's Gambit Accepted (QGA)
moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 dxc4 3. Nf3 Nf6 4. e3 e6 5. Bxc4 c5 6. O-O a6
description: Black accepts the gambit pawn temporarily, developing quickly and striking back at White's d4 center with ...c5 and ...a6-b5 queenside expansion.
keyIdeas: Avoid clinging to defend the c4 pawn
Strike at White's center with ...c5
Expand on the queenside with ...a6 and ...b5

name: Queen's Gambit Declined: Orthodox Defense
moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5 Be7 5. e3 O-O 6. Nf3 Nbd7
description: The bedrock of World Championship chess. Black solidly anchors d5 with ...e6 and completes harmonious kingside development.
keyIdeas: Impregnable d5 pawn anchor
Pin breaking with ...Be7 and castling
Prepare freeing maneuvers with ...c5 or ...e5

name: Queen's Gambit Declined: Exchange Variation
moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. cxd5 exd5 5. Bg5 c6 6. e3 Be7 7. Bd3 O-O
description: White trades on d5 to create the famous Carlsbad pawn structure, preparing a queenside Minority Attack (b4-b5) to create weaknesses in Black's pawn structure.
keyIdeas: Carlsbad pawn structure (a2-b2 vs a7-b7-c6)
Minority attack with b4-b5 to target c6
Black seeks kingside attacking counterplay

name: Queen's Gambit Declined: Tartakower Defense
moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5 Be7 5. e3 O-O 6. Nf3 h6 7. Bh4 b6
description: Garry Kasparov's trusted defense in World Championships. Black plays ...h6 and ...b6 to develop the problem light-squared bishop onto b7.
keyIdeas: Solve the bad light-squared bishop by fianchettoing on b7
Ask White's bishop questions with 6...h6
Harmonious piece coordination with counterplay on c5

name: Slav Defense: Main Line
moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 c6 3. Nf3 Nf6 4. Nc3 dxc4 5. a4 Bf5
description: Black supports d5 with ...c6 rather than ...e6, keeping the c8-h3 diagonal open for the bishop to emerge to f5 before locking the pawn chain.
keyIdeas: Develop bishop actively to f5
White plays a4 to prevent Black from holding c4 with ...b5
Ultra-solid pawn structure with active piece play

name: Semi-Slav Defense: Meran Variation
moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 c6 3. Nf3 Nf6 4. Nc3 e6 5. e3 Nbd7 6. Bd3 dxc4 7. Bxc4 b5 8. Bd3 a6
description: One of the most complex, theoretical openings in elite chess. Black builds a solid triangle (c6-d5-e6) then expands with ...b5 and ...a6 preparing ...c5.
keyIdeas: Pawn triangle on c6-d5-e6
Queenside pawn storm with ...b5, ...a6, and ...c5 break
Razor-sharp tactical middlegames

name: Albin Counter-Gambit
moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e5 3. dxe5 d4 4. Nf3 Nc6
description: A sharp, combative gambit. Black sacrifices a pawn with 2...e5 to plant a thorn pawn on d4 that cramps White's piece development.
keyIdeas: Establish the cramping d4 wedge
Dangerous opening traps (Lasker Underpromotion Trap)
High tactical volatility and initiative for Black

name: Chigorin Defense
moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 Nc6 3. Nf3 Bg4 4. cxd5 Bxf3 5. gxf3 Qxd5 6. e3 e5
description: Mikhail Chigorin's dynamic concept. Black develops knights quickly and pins White with ...Bg4, prioritizing piece activity and open lines over pawn rules.
keyIdeas: Rapid piece play with Nc6 and Bg4
Pressure White's d4 and c4 pawns immediately
Imbalanced positions with dynamic counter-attacking chances

name: Queen's Gambit: Ragozin Defense
moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Nf3 Bb4 5. cxd5 exd5 6. Bg5 h6
description: A top-tier modern defense favored by Levon Aronian and Daniil Dubov. Black pins White's knight on c3 with ...Bb4 and generates active central piece pressure.
keyIdeas: Pin Nc3 with ...Bb4
Combine QGD solidity with Nimzo-Indian piece activity
Flexible pawn structure with active counterplay
